newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova, Ukraine pledge to form customs union.
newsitem.headline: Moldova, Ukraine pledge to form customs union.

text.p: Presidents Leonid Kuchma of Ukraine and Petru Lucinschi of Moldova pledged on Tuesday to form an "equal" customs union removing many barriers between their countries.
The move is likely to be seen as rivalling Russian-led pacts with other former Soviet republics which Moldova and Ukraine have kept out of.
"We are taking a step towards a higher level of relations. Many barriers are being removed," Kuchma said after signing a signed a customs union declaration in the Moldovan capital.
Neither president referred specifically to customs deals between Russia and other former Soviet republics, but the agreement underlined their sensitivities over ties with Moscow.

"There is one thing that is different about our union -- it is a union of equal states, equal sides. This is its essence," Kuchma said of the union, under which transit fees and duties are to be lifted between the neighbouring countries.
Lucinschi, elected three months ago on promises of better ties with Russia, said the union was not aimed against anyone.

"Our will to form a customs union doesn't damage any third country. It will only help to develop ties, for instance, with Russia or Belarus," Lucinschi said of the deal, due to come into force by the end of the year.

Ukraine and Moldova have been sceptical about fast and deep integration in the 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States, formed on the ashes of the Soviet Union, and have not joined a customs union of Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
Ukraine, which has a population of more than 50 million, has criticised a "community" planned by Russia and Belarus in their drive for closer integration.

"There are many stages, many levels (of integration) but everything is run by Russian representatives," Leonid Derkach, head of Ukraine's Customs Service, told reporters. "Our union in fact signifies a free economic zone between two countries."

Ukraine has been a supporter of territorial integrity in Moldova, a country of less than five million people which has been hit by the de facto secession of the Dnestr region in 1990 and a war with Slav separatists there two years later.
Russian troops ended the bloodshed but Dnestr still has independent structures.
Kuchma said Ukraine, which with Russia helps mediate talks led by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, wanted more active role in settling the problems in Dnestr.
He said Kiev would allow 500,000 tonnes of arms stored in Dnestr be be transported through Ukraine to Russia under the guard of a 6,000-strong Russian military contingent.
Sources in the Ukrainian delegation told Reuters that Kiev was considering sending observers to Dnestr and might deploy a small number of peacekeeping troops.
Ukraine and Moldova have been working on delimitation of their 1,200-km (700-mile) border and Kuchma said the issue of three disputed border points would be resolved by July.
The main sticking point is at Giurgiulesti near the Romanian border, where Moldova owns a stretch of the Danube of about several hundreds metres (yards).
Chisinau wants to build an oil terminal there, while Ukraine fears it could reduce the importance of Ukraine's Danube ports.
